$comment: GENERATED by `pnpm bundle-sizes --write`. Do not hand-edit measured values. `tier`, `hardCeiling` and `note` ARE hand-maintained and are preserved across regeneration. A new entry needs a hand-written `tier` and `note` before `--write` can measure it. Policy: docs/contributing/conventions/bundle-budgets.md

index.js.note: kernel barrel; every consumer pays. Must not pull the observability subgraph — see the dedicated test.

client.js.note: browser client; must stay tiny. No kernel modules in the closure.

client-react.js.note: browser client + React hooks. React itself is external.

cloudflare.js.note: Worker isolate cold start. Aggregator: closure includes the index.js and http.js subgraphs, so growth that slips past those entries still surfaces here.

s3.js.note: Worker-safe S3 entry, so consumer-facing. Demonstrated catch: fast-xml-parser is pinned at 5.8.0 because 5.9.3 inflated this closure ~25%.

gcs.js.note: Worker-safe GCS entry, so consumer-facing. Smaller than s3.js because the GOOG4 signer is lighter than aws4fetch.

http.js.note: server-side. Also inside the cloudflare.js closure, so growth here shows up on that entry too.

auth.js.note: server-side. Reached from the index.js closure. Adding a fourth verifier grows this, not the kernel's.

maintenance.js.note: operator-side; reached from the cloudflare.js closure.

observability.js.note: operator-side. LogTape accounts for the bulk.

app-config.js.note: types erase and defineConfig is `<C>(c: C) => c`. The ceiling asserts THIS ENTRY HAS NO RUNTIME CLOSURE; a percentage gate on 167 B would be meaningless.

dev.js.note: dev-only; never enters a consumer bundle. At the 2% shipped rate it produced 12 of 32 historical trips for no safety benefit.

node.js.note: server-only aggregator. Raw-only dep-creep tripwire; live-external-import creep is caught separately by the bare-specifier allowlist test.

dev-vite.js.note: dev-only aggregator. Raw-only dep-creep tripwire; see node.js.
